feed.title: BYD inquires about Stellantis's shuttered 2.95M-sq-ft Brampton plant as 3,000 displaced workers wait for answers
feed.summary: Chinese EV manufacturer BYD Co. has expressed interest in acquiring Stellantis NV's closed assembly plant in Brampton, ON, potentially converting it into a transit bus production facility. This development comes as approximately 3,000 workers remain displaced since the plant's December 2023 shutdown, with Unifor criticizing Stellantis for moving planned production to the U.S. While other entities, including Leapmotor International and Canadian defense contractors, have also inquired, the future of the site and its workforce remains uncertain due to retooling challenges and the need for union involvement.

feed.title: The return of Sherwin-Williams’ workers may revive downtown Cleveland — but not without resistance
feed.summary: Sherwin-Williams' new downtown Cleveland headquarters is requiring employees to return to the office five days a week, a move welcomed by city officials hoping to revive the downtown area, but met with resistance from employees who had grown accustomed to remote work flexibility. The city had offered Sherwin-Williams a substantial incentive package to keep jobs and tax revenue in Cleveland, and the return-to-office mandate is seen as crucial for supporting local businesses and the urban core economy. This situation highlights the tension between corporate desires for collaboration, a city's need for economic revitalization, and employees' preferences for work-life balance established during the pandemic.

feed.title: The Discontinued Campbell's Pasta So Good, Fans Made A Facebook Page To Bring It Back (Sorry, Chef Boyardee)
feed.summary: Fans of Campbell's RavioliOs have expressed significant disappointment and started a Facebook group after the company discontinued the popular canned pasta. Many preferred RavioliOs over Chef Boyardee due to its distinct round shape and tangier sauce, and its discontinuation has sparked a strong reaction rooted in nostalgia. The brand has a long history, originally under Franco-American, which was acquired by Campbell's in 1915.
